productLossClosed: The shared headless draft policy remains local-first: repeated New Thread actions reuse one project-scoped draft and do not create durable thread rows.
The Native host now removes every canonical untouched New thread shell found in the initial server snapshot, including recently created leftovers, instead of retaining them for 24 hours.
Automatic recovery remains conservative: any non-default title, user message, turn, session, pending approval, pending user input, actionable plan, or archived state prevents deletion.
If recovery removes every canonical thread, the app still renders a usable New Thread hero with the project model, effort, runtime, interaction mode, checkout context, and normal Composer geometry.
rootCause: The earlier recovery policy required an untouched canonical shell to be at least 24 hours old.

A legacy or concurrently running old bundle could therefore create several empty canonical shells that remained visible for the rest of the day even though current New Thread entry points were already local-first.
safetyBoundary: Automatic recovery runs only for a complete initial or reconnected shell snapshot, never for incremental shell events.
The Web Implement plan two-phase flow uses a business title rather than New thread, and Mobile uses atomic turn bootstrap, so neither matches the recovery predicate.
Deletion uses the typed thread.delete command and failed commands are unhidden for retry.
The source ~/.t3-lynxtron database was opened read-only; every mutation occurred in disposable copies.
classification.evidenceBoundary: The fresh multi-empty fixture deliberately adjusts timestamps and adds one projection row in a disposable copy to exercise the newly closed time boundary. It proves startup recovery behavior, not that the current client can generate those rows. The empty-only fixture proves the reverse state after all canonical shells are removed.
